title: Build the Mermaid C4 diagram parser (C4 Diagrams component)
description:
Architecture blueprints draw their structure as Mermaid C4 diagrams, and
nothing in the CLI can read them. [[adr-029]] measured that the one Go
library with a C4 parser (`github.com/sammcj/mermaid-check` v0.5.1)
rejects this repository's own diagrams — it fails on
`Component(x, "X", "Go package (planned)", "desc")` — so the CLI gets a
parser of its own.

Add a new package under `cli/core` realizing the **C4 Diagrams**
component: it takes the content of one fenced `mermaid` block plus the
block's position in its document, and returns the diagram type and a
list of located statements. It is pure notation — it never reads the
corpus and never resolves a node to an element. Element resolution and
the checks are later items.

Blueprint: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-blueprint.md`, section "C4 Diagrams in [[module-document-core]]
(added)" — delta key PARSE. FRD: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-frd.md`, its Terminology table
lists the statement subset.

**ACs:** proves AC-C4-DIAG-001.2 (unit) and AC-C4-DIAG-004.1 (unit) —
this item owes the `// AC:` citation comments per
`specs/standards/ac-traceability-standards.md`. Participates in
AC-C4-DIAG-001.1, 001.3, 002.5, 003.1, 003.2, 004.2, 004.3 and 004.5,
which are proved by the check items in stage 2.

**Verification timing:** the participating ACs above are proved by the
items "Raise the c4 parse and node findings" and "Raise the c4
relationship and tag findings" in the stage-2 epic. Code here may
proceed now; those ACs are verified when that epic lands.

**Anchors:** `cli/core/span` (`Of`) computes every position;
`cli/core/markdown` (`Fenced`) is how a caller reaches the blocks and is
not called from this package; `cli/core/gherkin` is the precedent for a
notation parser living in Document Core.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Follow the blueprint's PARSE behavior lines exactly; they pin every
observable choice:

- Diagram type from the first statement; parse only `C4Context`,
  `C4Container`, `C4Component`. Any other first statement (including
  `C4Dynamic`, `C4Deployment`, `flowchart`) returns its type name and no
  statements.
- One statement per line. Skip blank lines and lines whose first
  non-blank characters are `%%`.
- Macros read: `System`, `Container`, `Component` and their `Db`/`Queue`
  forms; `Person` and every `_Ext` form (external nodes);
  `Boundary`, `Enterprise_Boundary`, `System_Boundary`,
  `Container_Boundary` (a boundary line ends with `{`, a line holding
  only `}` closes the innermost open boundary); `Rel`, `Rel_U`, `Rel_Up`,
  `Rel_D`, `Rel_Down`, `Rel_L`, `Rel_Left`, `Rel_R`, `Rel_Right`,
  `Rel_Back`, `BiRel`; ignored: `title`, `UpdateElementStyle`,
  `UpdateRelStyle`, `UpdateLayoutConfig`.
- Classify each statement: element node, external node, boundary,
  relationship, ignored.
- Arguments: a quoted argument runs to the next `"` (no escapes), so
  commas and parentheses inside are text; an unquoted argument is its
  trimmed text; `$<name>=<value>` is a named parameter and takes no
  positional slot.
- Positional order: `Rel*` — from, to, label, technology, description,
  sprite, tags, link. `Container*`/`Component*` — alias, label,
  technology, description, sprite, tags, link. `System*`/`Person*` —
  alias, label, description, sprite, tags, link.
- A statement outside the subset, with unbalanced quotes or parentheses,
  or with too few arguments for its macro is a parse error carrying that
  statement's span; parsing continues on the next line.
- Tags: read from the tags argument (positional or `$tags`), split on `+`
  only. `sync`, `async` and `contract:<slug>` are reserved (slug
  separated out); all others are unreserved, in written order. Record
  whether the argument contained a comma; `async,audited` is then one
  unreserved tag.
- Normalise to dependency direction: `Rel_Back(a, b)` → source b,
  target a. Directional variants are returned as `Rel` keeping the macro
  as written. `BiRel` is a relationship flagged bidirectional.
- Every span comes from `span.Of`, in whole-document coordinates.

Choose the package name and exported shapes yourself (anchors, not
signatures). Keep the parser table-driven so the subset can grow.

Fold: add **C4 Diagrams** to the Components section of `{DC}` under its
own `### C4 Diagrams` heading, with this record block, and add its node
to that section's C4Component diagram:

```component
entity_name: C4 Diagrams
slug: component-c4-diagrams
description: Mermaid C4 diagram parsing into located statements, with relationship tags read
```

Run `go test ./core/...` from `cli/`.
acceptance: A new cli/core package parses C4Context, C4Container and C4Component blocks into located statements per the PARSE delta's behavior lines, and returns the type name alone for any other diagram type.
A unit test proves AC-C4-DIAG-001.2: Component(x, "X", "Go package (planned), internal", "desc") parses with no error, the comma and parentheses kept inside the technology argument.
A unit test proves AC-C4-DIAG-004.1: Rel(a, b, "Uses", "HTTP", "", "", "async+audited") and Rel(a, b, "Uses", "HTTP", $tags="async+audited") both yield reserved tag async and unreserved tag audited.

Unit tests cover parse errors (unknown macro, unbalanced quote, too few arguments) carrying the statement's span, Rel_Back normalisation, BiRel flagging, comma detection in tags, and boundary open/close.
Every one of this repository's four C4 diagrams (in specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md and both module blueprints) parses with no error.
The C4 Diagrams component, with its record block and diagram node, is added to specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md.
go test ./core/... passes from cli/.

metadata.tier_reason: New parser with a deliberately narrow grammar, span arithmetic every later check depends on, and many pinned edge cases.

title: Declare the c4 rule identifiers and their finding detail variants
description:
The C4 diagram checks report under ten new rule identifiers, and `--only`
selects them by identifier, so the identifiers and each rule's
structured detail are a published surface that must exist before any
check raises them.

Declare in `cli/core/finding/finding.go`: `c4/parse`,
`c4/undeclared-node`, `c4/ambiguous-node`, `c4/bidirectional`,
`c4/duplicate-edge`, `c4/drawing-conflict`, `c4/interaction-conflict`,
`c4/contract-unresolved`, `c4/contract-mismatch`, `c4/tag-separator`.
Add their detail variants to the `FindingDetail` union in
`schemas/finding.strata` and regenerate.

Blueprint: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-blueprint.md`, section "Findings in [[module-document-core]]
(modified — c4 rules)" — delta key FIND.

003.2, 003.3, 004.2, 004.3 and 004.5; owes no citation. They are proved
by the two check items in the stage-2 epic, which is when they are
verified.

**Environment:** this item edits a `.strata` schema and must run `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`, which needs the `strata` compiler. A session without `STRATA_ACCESS_TOKEN` cannot install it (see `AGENTS.md`, "strata CLI"); do not hand-edit the generated files.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.

design:

title: C4 prerequisites: register and record component record blocks
description:
Stage 2 of C4 diagram conformance cannot run until un-promoted
components are visible in the index. Today `specs index` on this
repository records zero record blocks, so every component node on its
diagrams would be reported as undeclared and the profile
self-application test (`cli/profile/self_application_test.go`, which
requires zero findings) would fail.

Three things must land, in this order:

1. `agent-plugins-f6tl.5` — "Let a profile register record-block tags"
   (existing, structure feature). The host extension point.
2. This epic's child "Register the component record-block tag in the
   spec-driven-dev profile" — FEAT-SPECSTR-004's registration, which had
   no work order.
3. `agent-plugins-f6tl.6` — "Record registered record blocks and attach
   them to their heading" (existing, structure feature), including the
   decoding function the C4 element resolver uses.

The two existing beads stay children of the structure epic
`agent-plugins-f6tl`; this epic owns only the registration item.

**Edits to existing beads this file cannot carry** (run them once the
beads are imported; each is justified by the bead's own text):

- `bd undefer agent-plugins-f6tl.5 agent-plugins-f6tl.6` — both are
  deferred and are now on the critical path.
- `bd dep add <id of the registration item> agent-plugins-f6tl.5` —
  the registration uses the extension point f6tl.5 adds.
- `bd dep add agent-plugins-f6tl.6 <id of the registration item>` —
  f6tl.6 says it lands after this registration and had no edge for it.

Sources: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-blueprint.md` (Sequencing Constraints, stage 2; Tracker
Reconciliation), `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`
(deltas XPT and REC), `specs/features/structure-conformance/structure-conformance-frd.md`
(FEAT-SPECSTR-004).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All three items have landed.
- [ ] `specs index` on this repository records a `component` record
      block for every `component` fence in the container and module
      blueprints' Components sections.

title: Widen the Profile extension point with an architecture vocabulary
description:
Document Core must find C4 elements — systems, containers, modules,
components — without naming a document type, a frontmatter property or
a heading, because `cli/core` may hold no framework vocabulary (the
source-scan test `TestTheExtensionPointNamesNoRegisteredVocabulary`
enforces it). Per [[adr-030]], the `Profile` interface in
`cli/core/corpus/profile.go` gains one member carrying that vocabulary,
as `FeatureTags()` carries the Gherkin vocabulary.

Blueprint: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-blueprint.md`, section "Profile extension point in
[[module-document-core]] (modified — C4)" — delta key XPT.

**ACs:** participates in AC-C4-DIAG-002.1 and AC-C4-DIAG-004.4; owes no
citation. They are proved by the two check items in this epic.

**Anchors:** `cli/core/corpus/profile.go` (`Profile`,
`FeatureTagRules` as the precedent); `cli/core/corpus/registration.go`
(`ValidateRegistration`, `RegistrationDefect`).

## Retro

one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused

design:
The member carries:
- the document types that declare an element, each with a C4 level
  (`system`, `container`, `module`, `component`);
- the entity-name property; the system property; the composed-modules
  property; the consumed-contracts property; the contract document type

title: Build the C4 element set and resolve diagram nodes (C4 Elements component)
description:
A diagram node is valid only if it names a declared element, and which
elements it may name depends on the document it is drawn in. Add a new
package under `cli/core` realizing the **C4 Elements** component: it
builds the corpus's element set from architecture blueprints and roster
record blocks, computes each drawing document's scope, and resolves
each node to the elements its label names. The checks in this epic and
the C4 model feature both read it, so they cannot disagree about what a
node is.

Blueprint: `specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-blueprint.md`, section "C4 Elements in [[module-document-core]]
(added — node resolution)" — delta key ELEM. FRD terminology ("Element",
"Entity name", "Scope of a drawing document", "Passive store") is in
`specs/features/spec-c4-diagrams/spec-c4-diagrams-frd.md`.

**ACs:** participates in AC-C4-DIAG-001.4, 002.1, 002.2, 002.3, 002.4
and 002.5; owes no citation (proved by "Raise the c4 parse and node
findings").

**Anchors:** `cli/core/corpus` (`Corpus.Entry`, the index's
`RecordBlock` and `Heading` records); `cli/core/markdown`
(`Identifier`, `Fenced`); the record-block decoding function
`agent-plugins-f6tl.6` adds; the C4 Diagrams package from the stage-1
epic.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
All values come from the registered architecture vocabulary; name none
in code.

- An element per corpus member whose type is registered, slug = the
  member's slug, name = its entity-name property.
- An element per record block whose tag is the roster tag registered for
  the document's type and which is attached to the roster heading or a
  heading nested in its section. Match the heading on
  `markdown.Identifier`, so case does not decide.
- Decode roster blocks with the structure feature's decoding function. A
  block that does not decode to a mapping with a slug and entity name
  declares nothing (reporting it is the structure checks' job).
- Record blocks in a type with no roster (e.g. a feature blueprint's
  delta block) declare nothing.
- One element per slug, holding every declaration (blueprint
  frontmatter and/or record blocks), ordered by path then span.
- Scope of a drawing document: its own element; its roster's elements,
  by record block or by a body reference resolving to a component-level
  member and placed under the roster heading; the elements its
  composed-modules property names; every system- and container-level
  element in the corpus.
- A node resolves to every in-scope element whose name equals its label
  exactly, as written. External nodes are not resolved. A `Db`/`Queue`
  node matching nothing in scope is a passive store.
- Diagrams in a member whose type is not registered yield no nodes.
- Diagrams are read from the blueprint's source at run time; do not add
  them to the index (no index shape change, no `schema_version` change).

Fold: add **C4 Elements** to the Components section of
`specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md`, under
`### C4 Elements`, with this record block and a diagram node:

